newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lebed says Russia will be in post-IFOR force.
newsitem.headline: Lebed says Russia will be in post-IFOR force.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed said on Tuesday Russia would take part in any follow-on force to the NATO-led peace mission in Bosnia which ends in December.
"Yes, Russia will participate, we will play a serious part," he told reporters at NATO's military headquarters in southern Belgium.

Lebed was replying to questions after visiting the control room for the 55,000-strong multinational force in Bosnia which has been overseeing implementation of the Dayton peace accords which ended the 3-1/2 year war.
Russia has about 2,000 troops in the force and a Russian liaison officer at NATO's military command centre at Mons in southern Belgium.
NATO defence ministers agreed last month to begin drawing up plans for a follow-on force when the current Implementation Force (IFOR) mandate runs out in December.

Most countries accept such a force, although smaller, will be necessary to stop the country sliding back into war, but the issue is highly sensitive ahead of November's presidential elections in the United States.
Russia has about 2,000 troops in the 55,000-strong force, a contribution seen as a forerunner of future links between the alliance and Moscow.
At Mons, the Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, a Russian liaison officer has an office next to U.S. General George Joulwan, the top NATO commander.
NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana has proposed assigning Russian liaison officers at virtually all levels of the alliance's command structure in order to quell Moscow's fears of expansion.
